x: K.C. Pant was the Chairman of the 10th Finance Commission.

x: A.M. Khusro chaired the 11th Finance Commission.

s: Who chaired the 12th Finance Commission?
x: C. Rangarajan was the Chairman of the 12th Finance Commission.

x: The 1st Finance Commission was chaired by K.C. Neogy and covered the period 1952–57.

s: Which one of the following correctly gives the award period of the 10th Finance Commission?
x: The award period of the 10th Finance Commission was 1995–2000.

s: The award period of the 11th Finance Commission was:
x: The 11th Finance Commission covered 2000–05.
tq: Use chronological sequencing of adjacent award periods.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the award period of the 12th Finance Commission?
x: The 12th Finance Commission had the award period 2005–10.

s: The 13th Finance Commission covered the period:
x: The award period of the 13th Finance Commission was 2010–15.

s: Which one of the following is the correct award period of the 14th Finance Commission?
x: The 14th Finance Commission covered 2015–20.
tq: Discriminate between the award period and nearby five-year alternatives.

s: The recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission covered which periods?
x: The 15th Finance Commission recommendations covered 2020–21 and 2021–26.
tq: Test the unusual split award period rather than assuming one continuous five-year period.

s: The award period of the 16th Finance Commission is:
x: The 16th Finance Commission covers 2026–27 to 2030–31.

s:
With reference to the Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It is constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution.
2. It is a quasi-judicial constitutional body.
3. It is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Article 280 provides for a quasi-judicial Finance Commission constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
tq: Verify the constitutional article, institutional character and periodicity together.

s: The Finance Commission consists of:
o: A Chairman and four members appointed by the President
A Chairman and three members appointed by Parliament
A Chairman and four members appointed by the Prime Minister
x: The Finance Commission comprises a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President.
tq: Test composition and appointing authority in the same question.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the members of the Finance Commission:
1. Their term is specified by the President.
2. They are eligible for reappointment.
3. Their term is fixed permanently by the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The President specifies the term, and members are eligible for reappointment. The Constitution does not permanently prescribe one fixed term.
tq: Identify the true provisions and reject the absolute claim about a permanently fixed term.

s: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are prescribed by Parliament under the:
x: Parliament prescribed the qualifications through the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, also referred to in abbreviated form as the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
tq: Distinguish the exact statutory title from plausible but nonexistent titles.

s: Which of the following is the prescribed qualification for the Chairman of the Finance Commission?
o: Service as a Governor of a State
Experience exclusively as a High Court Chief Justice
Membership of Parliament for ten years
x: The Chairman must have experience in public affairs.
tq: Match the office with its exact statutory qualification rather than a prestigious but unstated qualification.

s: Which one of the following is NOT among the specified fields from which the four members of the Finance Commission are drawn?
o: A person with special knowledge of international diplomacy
A High Court judge or a person qualified to be one
A person with wide experience in financial administration
An expert in government finance and accounts
x: The specified fields include judicial qualification, government finance and accounts, financial administration, and economics. International diplomacy is not one of them.
tq: Find the one field outside the statutory list of member qualifications.

s: Which of the following correctly states the nature of the recommendations of the Finance Commission?
o: They have the force of constitutional amendments.
They are binding on the Union Government in all circumstances.
They are advisory and are not binding.
They are binding only on State Governments.
x: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory and not binding.
tq: Discriminate between advisory and binding constitutional recommendations.

s: P.V. Rajamannar observed that the recommendations of the Finance Commission:
o: Can be modified only by the Supreme Court
May be rejected without assigning any reason
Are automatically enforceable as judicial decrees
Should not be rejected without very compelling reasons
x: P.V. Rajamannar stated that the recommendations should not be rejected without very compelling reasons.
tq: Recall the precise qualification attached to the advisory nature of recommendations.

s: Under Article 281, the President is required to place before each House of Parliament:
o: Only the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
The recommendations along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken
The recommendations after approval by the Supreme Court
x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s recommendations together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken before each House of Parliament.
tq: Test the constitutional procedure and watch for the omission of the explanatory memorandum.

s: Which Article provides for the Finance Commission, while Article 290 deals with pensions?
x: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, whereas Article 290 deals with pensions. Article 281 concerns laying the recommendations before Parliament.
tq: Separate the look-alike constitutional article numbers by their subjects.

s: Which of the following correctly shows the States’ share of central taxes recommended by the 10th to 13th Finance Commissions?
x: The respective shares were 29% under the 10th, 29.5% under the 11th, 30.5% under the 12th and 32% under the 13th Finance Commission.
tq: Read the sequence across the comparison table without reversing adjacent percentages.
sec: Share of central taxes recommended (10th onward)  [APPSC]

s: The share of central taxes recommended by the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions was respectively:
x: Both the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions recommended a 41% share for the States.
tq: Distinguish the reduction under the 15th Commission from the unchanged figure under the 16th.
sec: Share of central taxes recommended (10th onward)  [APPSC]

s: The 10th Finance Commission’s sharing of all central taxes was implemented through the 80th Constitutional Amendment, 2000, with effect from:
x: The 80th Amendment, 2000 implemented the 10th Finance Commission’s sharing of all central taxes with effect from 1 April 1996.
tq: Separate the amendment year from its effective date.
sec: Share of central taxes recommended (10th onward)  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following sequence of States’ share of central taxes:
1. 42%
2. 41%
3. 41%
This sequence corresponds to the recommendations of the:
x: The 14th Finance Commission recommended 42%, while the 15th and 16th recommended 41% each.
tq: Track the numerical trend from the peak to the unchanged later figure.
sec: Share of central taxes recommended (10th onward)  [APPSC]

s: The reduction in the States’ share from 42% under the 14th Finance Commission to 41% under the 15th Finance Commission was attributed to:
o: The abolition of the divisible pool
The introduction of the GDP criterion
Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory
x: The reduction was attributed to Jammu and Kashmir becoming a Union Territory.
tq: Link the change in percentage to the specific institutional change responsible for it.
sec: Share of central taxes recommended (10th onward)  [APPSC]

s: The 14th Finance Commission was constituted on:
x: The 14th Finance Commission was constituted on 2 January 2013.
tq: Distinguish the constitution date from the date of acceptance and implementation.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: Which major change was associated with the 14th Finance Commission?
o: A shift towards tax devolution as the main route, along with ignoring the Plan/non-Plan distinction
A shift from tax devolution to exclusive grants
Introduction of the GDP criterion for the first time
x: The 14th Finance Commission made tax devolution the main route instead of grants and ignored the Plan/non-Plan distinction.
tq: Test the direction of policy change by contrasting devolution with grants.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: Under the 14th Finance Commission’s allocation formula for local-body grants, the weights assigned to the 2011 population and area were respectively:
x: The allocation was based on the 2011 population with a 90% weight and area with a 10% weight.
tq: Recall the exact pair of weights and their order.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following was an additional consideration introduced by the 15th Finance Commission?
x: The 15th Finance Commission retained the 41% share and added demographic performance and tax effort as considerations.
tq: Identify the new criteria rather than a feature associated with an earlier commission.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: The 15th Finance Commission used which population base in its recommendations?
x: The 15th Finance Commission used the 2011 population base.
tq: Test the exact population reference and avoid substituting an earlier census year.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission:
1. It retained the States’ share at 41%.
2. It introduced a contribution to GDP criterion carrying a 10% weight.
3. It discontinued revenue-deficit grants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The 16th Finance Commission retained 41%, introduced the GDP criterion with a 10% contribution and discontinued revenue-deficit grants.
tq: Combine percentage, criterion and grant-policy facts in one coded statement question.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: What contribution to the criteria was assigned to the new GDP criterion by the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The new GDP criterion carried a 10% contribution.
tq: Test a small but high-risk numerical detail directly.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: The total grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission amounted to:
x: The 16th Finance Commission recommended total grants of ₹9.47 lakh crore.
tq: Distinguish the exact total grant figure from nearby numerical distractors.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly represents the 16th Finance Commission’s grants for rural and urban local bodies?
o: Rural ₹4.4 lakh crore; urban ₹4.4 lakh crore
Rural ₹4.4 lakh crore; urban ₹3.6 lakh crore
Rural ₹3.6 lakh crore; urban ₹3.6 lakh crore
Rural ₹3.6 lakh crore; urban ₹4.4 lakh crore
x: The 16th Finance Commission recommended ₹4.4 lakh crore for rural local bodies and ₹3.6 lakh crore for urban local bodies.
tq: Avoid reversing the rural and urban figures in a paired comparison.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: The urban share in the local-body grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission was:
x: The urban share was 45%.
tq: Test the percentage attached specifically to the urban component.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: The disaster corpus recommended by the 16th Finance Commission for SDRF and SDMF was:
x: The recommended disaster corpus was ₹2,04,401 crore for SDRF and SDMF.
tq: Check the exact crore figure and do not transpose its digits.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: The cost-sharing ratio for the disaster corpus recommended for North-Eastern and Himalayan States was:
x: For North-Eastern and Himalayan States, the cost-sharing ratio was 90:10.
tq: Match the special regional category with its distinct cost-sharing ratio.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: For States other than the North-Eastern and Himalayan States, the disaster-corpus cost-sharing ratio recommended by the 16th Finance Commission was:
x: The ratio for other States was 75:25.
tq: Contrast the general ratio with the special ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: Which two phenomena were proposed as new national disasters by the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Heatwaves and lightning were proposed as new notified national disasters.
tq: Recall the paired additions and reject familiar but unstated disaster categories.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: The 16th Finance Commission recommended that State deficits be capped at what percentage of GSDP?
x: State deficits were recommended to be capped at 3% of GSDP.
tq: Test the fiscal-limit percentage directly against close alternatives.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following grants were discontinued by the 16th Finance Commission?
o: Revenue-deficit grants, sector-specific grants and State-specific grants
All grants to rural local bodies
x: The 16th Finance Commission discontinued revenue-deficit grants, sector-specific grants and State-specific grants.
tq: Identify the complete set of discontinued grants without overextending the word “all”.
sec: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations  [APPSC]

s: In the context of Finance Commission devolution, the term ‘vertical distribution’ refers to:
o: Allocation of the States’ share among different States
Distribution of the divisible pool between the Union and the States
Distribution of grants among Panchayats and Municipalities
Allocation of State taxes between rural and urban local bodies
x: Vertical distribution refers to the share of the divisible pool transferred to the States from the Union. Horizontal distribution refers to allocation of that States’ share among individual States.
tq: Discriminate between two closely related terms by identifying the level at which distribution takes place.
sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

s: With reference to the divisible pool of central taxes, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It excludes the proceeds of all shareable taxes under Article 270.
It consists only of State taxes collected by the Union.
It includes all gross tax revenue, including cesses and surcharges.
It was approximately 81% of gross tax revenue in 2025–26.
x: The divisible pool comprises shareable taxes under Article 270, excluding cesses and surcharges. In 2025–26, it was approximately 81% of gross tax revenue.
tq: Separate the divisible pool from gross tax revenue by checking the stated proportion and exclusions.
sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following best describes ‘horizontal distribution’ by the Finance Commission?
o: Division of the divisible pool between the Union and the States
Division of a State’s revenue between the State Government and local bodies
Allocation of the States’ share among the States according to a formula
Distribution of the Consolidated Fund of India between the two Houses of Parliament
x: Horizontal distribution is the allocation among States of the share assigned to the States through a prescribed formula.
tq: Test the distinction between vertical and horizontal distribution by focusing on the recipients of the allocation.
sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the criteria used by the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commissions:
a. Income distance — 50% under the 14th FC; 45% under the 15th FC
b. Population 1971 — 17.5% under the 14th FC
c. Population 2011 — 10% under the 14th FC; 15% under the 15th FC
d. Area — 15% under both the 14th and 15th FCs
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The 14th FC gave weight to both 1971 and 2011 population, while the 15th FC used 2011 population and retained the 15% weight for area.
tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and verify whether the remaining criteria preserve their stated weights.
sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to the Sixteenth Finance Commission for 2026–31, consider the following statements:
1. Income distance has a weight of 42.5%.
2. Population 2011 has a weight of 17.5%.
3. Contribution to GDP has been introduced with a weight of 10%.
4. Tax and fiscal effort has been retained with a weight of 2.5%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: the Sixteenth Finance Commission dropped the 2.5% criterion for tax and fiscal effort.
tq: Find the dropped criterion before selecting the coded combination of retained weights.
sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, income distance is measured from:
o: The average of the top five States by population
The income of the poorest State alone
The average of the top three large States
The average income of all States
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission measures income distance from the average of the top three large States.
tq: Test the exact reference point used for a comparative fiscal criterion.
sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

s: The demographic performance criterion under the Sixteenth Finance Commission is based on:
o: The share of working-age population in 2026
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission bases demographic performance on population growth between 1971 and 2011, replacing the total fertility rate measure.
tq: Discriminate between the earlier fertility-rate measure and the later population-growth measure.
sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following changes in the treatment of forests is associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Open forest and the increase in forest area between 2015 and 2023 are included.
Only reserved forests are counted, excluding open forests.
Forest cover has been removed as a criterion altogether.
Only forest revenue collected by a State is considered.
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission includes open forest and the increase in forest area during 2015–2023 in its treatment of the forest criterion.
tq: Identify the precise expansion of a criterion rather than accepting an absolute or exclusive formulation.
sec: Vertical vs horizontal distribution; 15th FC weights  [APPSC]

s: What was Andhra Pradesh’s share of the States’ divisible pool under the Fifteenth Finance Commission?
x: Andhra Pradesh’s share was 4.05% under the Fifteenth Finance Commission. Its share was 4.305% under the Fourteenth and 4.217% under the Sixteenth Finance Commission.
tq: Distinguish closely spaced percentages by associating each figure with the correct Finance Commission period.

s: Which of the following correctly states the allocations for Andhra Pradesh under the Sixteenth Finance Commission for 2026–31?
o: Rural local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; urban local bodies: ₹12,158 crore; disaster: ₹6,125 crore
Rural local bodies: ₹12,158 crore; urban local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; disaster: ₹5,000 crore
Rural local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; urban local bodies: ₹6,125 crore; disaster: ₹12,158 crore
Rural local bodies: ₹5,000 crore; urban local bodies: ₹12,158 crore; disaster: ₹6,627 crore
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission allocation for Andhra Pradesh is ₹16,627 crore for rural local bodies, ₹12,158 crore for urban local bodies and ₹6,125 crore for disaster-related grants.
tq: Match each financial figure with its correct recipient category rather than relying on the size of the number alone.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding special urban grants under the Sixteenth Finance Commission:
1. Vijayawada is eligible for a special urban grant.
2. Visakhapatnam is eligible for a special urban grant.
3. Each of the two cities can receive up to ₹5,000 crore for wastewater systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam are both eligible for special urban grants, with each eligible to receive up to ₹5,000 crore for wastewater systems.
tq: Check whether the same eligibility condition applies to both named cities and whether the ceiling is correctly stated.

s: The discontinuation of revenue-deficit grants to Andhra Pradesh under the Sixteenth Finance Commission is associated with which stated fiscal position?
o: The State reduced its revenue deficit to 1.1% in Budget 2026–27.
The State’s fiscal deficit became equal to zero in Budget 2026–27.
The State increased its revenue deficit to 4.22% in Budget 2026–27.
The State eliminated all public debt by Budget 2026–27.
x: Revenue-deficit grants were stopped after Andhra Pradesh reduced its revenue deficit to 1.1% in Budget 2026–27.
tq: Link a fiscal outcome to the policy consequence without substituting a different deficit measure.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: It was rejected in Parliament in 2014 and replaced by a constitutional tax devolution formula.
It was included in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and implemented by the 14th Finance Commission.
It was promised in Parliament in 2014 but was not included in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act.
It was granted by the 15th Finance Commission through a separate constitutional amendment.
x: Special Category Status was promised in Parliament in 2014, but it was not included in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act. The 14th Finance Commission made no distinction between special and general category States, and the Centre offered special assistance instead.
tq: Separate a parliamentary assurance from statutory inclusion and subsequent Finance Commission treatment.

s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of their shares under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, using the figures given:
A. Andhra Pradesh — 4.217%
B. Uttar Pradesh — 17.619%
C. Bihar — 9.948%
D. Kerala — 2.382%
x: The descending order is Uttar Pradesh (17.619%), Bihar (9.948%), Andhra Pradesh (4.217%) and Kerala (2.382%).
tq: Use the largest and smallest figures first, then place the middle values by direct comparison.

s: Which of the following statements about the southern States under the Sixteenth Finance Commission is correct?
o: All five southern States received exactly the same percentage share.
Only Andhra Pradesh and Telangana gained, while the other southern States lost.
Karnataka and Tamil Nadu were excluded from the horizontal distribution formula.
All five southern States gained in their shares of the States’ pool.
x: All five southern States gained under the Sixteenth Finance Commission. The stated shares include Karnataka 4.131%, Kerala 2.382%, Tamil Nadu 4.097% and Telangana 2.174%.
tq: Test the comparative trend across a group before checking individual percentages.

s: Which Article requires the President to lay the report of the Finance Commission before each House of Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken?
x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s report before each House of Parliament together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken.
tq: Distinguish the Article dealing with presentation of the report from the Article establishing the Commission and its functions.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Commission:
1. Its recommendations are not binding on the Government.
2. Its recommendations cover cesses and surcharges as part of the divisible pool.
3. It may deal with matters referred to it by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false: cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool covered by the Finance Commission’s tax-sharing recommendations.
tq: Locate the exception in the scope of tax devolution and separate it from the Commission’s advisory character.

s: The State Finance Commission is constituted:
o: Only once after the formation of a State under Article 356
Every third year under Articles 280 and 281
Every fifth year under Articles 243-I and 243-Y
x: The State Finance Commission is constituted every fifth year under Articles 243-I and 243-Y to review the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities at the State level.
tq: Identify the State-level counterpart by combining its periodicity with its constitutional provisions.

s: The Finance Commission’s function of recommending measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State for supplementing the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities was added through the:
x: The relevant function was added by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, 1992, relating respectively to Panchayats and Municipalities.
tq: Associate the local-government finance function with the constitutional amendments that strengthened local self-government.

s: The financing of disaster management was included among the terms of reference of which Finance Commission?
x: Disaster-management financing under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, was included in the terms of reference of the Fifteenth Finance Commission.
tq: Use the named legislation and the specific Finance Commission to avoid confusing the terms of reference of successive Commissions.

s: The Terms of Reference of the 16th Finance Commission were approved by the Union Cabinet on which date?
x: The Terms of Reference of the 16th Finance Commission were approved by the Cabinet on 29 November 2023.
tq: Direct date recall using closely related Finance Commission dates.

s: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on:
x: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023.
tq: Distinguish the Cabinet approval date from the constitution date.

s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the 16th Finance Commission:
a. T. Rabi Sankar — Member
b. Annie George Mathew — Member
c. Manoj Panda — Member
d. Soumya Kanti Ghosh — Member
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: T. Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda and Soumya Kanti Ghosh are all members of the 16th Finance Commission.
tq: Use a complete membership list and test recognition of all correctly matched pairs.

s:
With reference to the 16th Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. Its Terms of Reference came directly from the Constitution without detailed Central directives.
2. It was constituted on 31 December 2023.
3. It was the first Finance Commission to use Contribution to GDP as a criterion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023, had constitution-based Terms of Reference, and was the first to use Contribution to GDP as a criterion.
tq: Combine constitutional, chronological and first-in-series facts in a coded statement question.

s: The report of the 16th Finance Commission was submitted to the President in:
x: The 16th Finance Commission submitted its report to the President in November 2025.
tq: Direct recall of a year-month fact with nearby event dates as distractors.

s: The report of the 16th Finance Commission was tabled in Parliament on:
x: The report was tabled in Parliament on 1 February 2026.
tq: Discriminate between closely spaced February 2026 dates.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the 16th Finance Commission is correct?
o: The Centre accepted the devolution recommended by it.
The Centre rejected its recommended devolution framework.
It recommended a 50 per cent share for all States.
It discontinued grants-in-aid to local bodies.
x: The Centre accepted the devolution recommended by the 16th Finance Commission. The demand for a 50 per cent share by 18 of 28 States was not accepted.
tq: Identify the correct institutional response while rejecting exaggerated alternatives.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Eighteen out of twenty-eight States sought a 50 per cent share.
2. The demand for a 50 per cent share was accepted by the Centre.
3. The 16th Finance Commission retained the States' share at 41 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the demand for a 50 per cent share was not accepted.
tq: Find the reversed decision in a numerical statement set.

s:

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: Sushma Nath was a member of the 14th Finance Commission. T. Rabi Sankar and Soumya Kanti Ghosh are associated with the 16th Finance Commission, while Abhijit Sen was a member of the 14th Commission.

s: The Government of India accepted the report of the 14th Finance Commission on:
x: The Government of India accepted the report of the 14th Finance Commission on 24 February 2015.
tq: Direct recall of an acceptance date distinct from the constitution date.

s: The increase in the States' share in the divisible pool recommended by the 14th Finance Commission was described as:
o: a temporary increase applicable for one year
x: The 14th Finance Commission's increase of the States' share to 42 per cent was the largest increase ever.
tq: Identify the precise comparative description rather than a numerical distractor.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the vertical devolution recommended by the 14th, 15th and 16th Finance Commissions respectively?
o: 41 per cent, 42 per cent, 41 per cent
42 per cent, 42 per cent, 50 per cent
32 per cent, 42 per cent, 41 per cent
42 per cent, 41 per cent, 41 per cent
x: The 14th Finance Commission recommended 42 per cent, while the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions retained or recommended 41 per cent.

s: The 15th Finance Commission was the first Finance Commission to:
o: cut the States' vertical share from 42 per cent to 41 per cent
recommend a 50 per cent share to the States
x: The 15th Finance Commission was the first to reduce the vertical share from 42 per cent to 41 per cent, largely in the context of the change in Jammu and Kashmir's status.
tq: Test a first-in-series fact against nearby but unsupported reforms.

s:
Consider the following statements about population criteria used by Finance Commissions:
1. The 14th Finance Commission used both the 1971 and 2011 population figures.
2. The 15th Finance Commission used the 2011 population figure.
3. The 16th Finance Commission measured demographic performance against the 1971 population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct regarding the population bases and demographic-performance measure of the three Commissions.

s: The Contribution to GDP criterion introduced by the 16th Finance Commission carries a weight of:
x: The 16th Finance Commission is the first to use Contribution to GDP as a criterion, with a weight of 10 per cent.
tq: Separate a criterion weight from devolution percentages and State shares.

s: Special Category Status was first granted in 1969 on the recommendation of the:
x: Special Category Status was first granted in 1969 on the recommendation of the 5th Finance Commission.
tq: Direct recall of the origin year and recommending body.
sec: Special Category Status - origin and criteria  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

s: Assistance under which formula favoured States enjoying Special Category Status?
